runs.name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc.; NYSE SEI, modular equipment for power generation, control and distribution for data center, energy and industrial customers (Solaris Power Solutions) and for raw-materials management in oil and gas well completions (Solaris Logistics Solutions); formerly Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure, renamed September 2024 after the Mobile Energy Rentals acquisition; Focus Genco bought 2026-03-16 for 4,182,772 Class A shares and about $81M cash, GESA 2026-07-01, Omega Foundation Services 2026-09-01 for 3,599,199 Class A shares and about $77M cash; an Up-C through Solaris Energy Infrastructure, LLC; the 10-K names no rival, Smart Sand, U.S. Silica, ProPetro, Liberty and Atlas read as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$65.16** (2026-10-15 close, through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **80,165,591** (10-Q cover, 0001628280-26-054349, `Screens/cover_shares.py`: Class A 65,831,540 and Class B 10,734,852 paired with OpCo units, one economic count; checked against 73,549 thousand issued at 2026-06-30, the GESA shares of 2026-07-01 after it; plus the 3,599,199 Omega shares of 2026-09-01, 8-K 0001193125-26-385257); cap **$5,224M**; face debt $2,547.7M at 2026-06-30 against cash $824.1M, $1,250M of 7.000% notes due 2032 added 2026-10-01; both convertibles in the money (about 18.9M shares, carried as debt). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001628280-26-012501) and the FY2018 to FY2024 10-Ks, the 10-Qs to 2026-06-30, the proxy (0001140361-26-012799), the Genco, Genco 8-K/A, Omega and notes 8-Ks; one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $209,104K, filed statement against `tools/run.py`). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. Balance sheets 2018 to 2026-06 read in Step 0: a nearly debt-free logistics company of $400M to $500M of assets 2018 to 2023, $4.2B by mid-2026, mostly turbines; shares about 43.0M to 80.2M in about two and a half years. **Which part decides, a CONVENTION of the run:** the business-of-parts rule names no window and no measure, and the filer reports only segment Adjusted EBITDA; on the last five fiscal years (2021 to 2025) logistics decides (about 59% of estimated operating profit, 65% of segment Adjusted EBITDA); on the trailing five years to the last 10-Q power decides (about 52%) and the file would close at Q1, TOO HARD (NATURE) (the 10-K: the distributed power industry "is evolving rapidly"); every forward measure says power is the business (80% of 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA, 87% of segment assets, nearly all capital spending, all the debt); no window makes it IN. Q1 IN on logistics (patented wellsite sand-storage systems rented out, eight filed years through a full cycle). **Q2 OUT** on logistics: a castle open on the evidence protecting only ordinary returns over the full cycle; some customers use "their own equipment" and rivals bundle sand, storage and delivery; profit per system about $1.0M in 2019, $0.96M in 2025, $0.91M annualized in the first half of 2026, falling through the inflation; segment Adjusted EBITDA down three years running ($115.1M, $97.6M, $88.9M); 9.3% pre-tax on tangible assets 2017 to 2023, 6.4% peak to peak. The 10-K names no rival; Smart Sand 0.2% (2017 to 2025), U.S. Silica 0.0% (2017 to 2023), ProPetro 2.3%, Liberty 9.9% (2017 to 2025) and Atlas 10.5% (2022 to 2025, -0.6% in 2025) pre-tax operating income on tangible assets, read as a CONVENTION of the run. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the Morpheus short-seller report of 2025-03-17 and the Pirello securities class action over the MER acquisition, dismissed voluntarily without prejudice; related parties (Solaris Energy Management, owned by the Chairman and Co-CEO) and a charter letting "Designated Parties", Zartler among them, compete with the company; Co-CEO pay $3.8M to $13.9M in 2025; a Tax Receivable Agreement paying 85% of tax savings, $109.2M payable. Against the power part, after the stop: one data-center customer 88% of power revenue in 2025 and the 49.9% partner in Stateline; one leading generation-equipment supplier; customers who may need power only until line power arrives; $926.5M of growth spending 2021 to 2025 earning about 5.6% after tax. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash after all spending five-year mean -$147.8M (2025 -$477.7M); depreciation as maintenance central, $35.2M a year all-equity, $30.7M after interest; value **about -$16.4 to -$16.3** a share all-equity against $65.16 (equity-only $5.98 to $6.07); the floor needs about $718M a year against $35.2M, no case earns it; fair price **about -$20.8 all-equity** (about $2.1 equity-only beside); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing showing the HMH, NGS, NOV, OIS and USAC run files of 2026-10-16, none opened; the NGS commit subjects and AYI and ARCB research-folder names in the session context; a memory index line naming no SEI verdict; none used. Commits fb099ef8, 8a681946, af57ab87, 77637939, 73c1f790, ac9712fd, six. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for SEI, SOI or Solaris). Citations: the analyst's citation check PASS (43 ids, 42 quoted fragments); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` no phantom, no E-id and no slip among 33 tight pairs; the wider sweep's misses are filing quotations and the framework's own wording, none set beside a ledger id as the row's words. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the business-of-parts rule names no window and no measure, and here the choice moves the deciding part from logistics to power (a company in transformation: which window, which measure, and whether the part carrying most of the capital and the debt matters at Q1 whatever its past profit); (2) no rule for a non-deciding part whose future cannot be judged; (3) Q7 (e) gives no method for charging growth spending, charged here at the 5.6% it earned, a CONVENTION of the run; (4) "Whose tax" says nothing of a Tax Receivable Agreement. Could not get: segment operating profit (estimated), MER's pre-merger statements, the Morpheus report itself, the July 2026 Hatchbo agreement, GESA and Omega financials, interest paid 2021 to 2022 (taken as nil).
runs.narr: Q2 OUT on the deciding part, logistics (the fiscal five-year window, a CONVENTION of the run): a castle open on the evidence protecting only ordinary returns over the full cycle; customers using their own equipment, rivals bundling sand, storage and delivery, profit per system falling through the inflation, segment Adjusted EBITDA down three years running, 9.3% pre-tax on tangible assets 2017 to 2023; the rivals read a CONVENTION of the run, the 10-K naming none. On the trailing window power decides and the file closes at Q1, TOO HARD (NATURE); no window makes it IN. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the Morpheus short report and a class action dismissed without prejudice, related parties and a charter letting Designated Parties compete, Co-CEO pay $3.8M to $13.9M, a TRA paying 85% of tax savings. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value about -$16.4 to -$16.3 a share all-equity against $65.16, fair about -$20.8 all-equity ($2.1 equity-only), not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: the parts rule's window and measure for a company in transformation; a non-deciding part that cannot be judged; the method of charging growth spending at Q7 (e); the Tax Receivable Agreement under Whose tax.
